title: Protocol for the generation and immunostaining of thick murine lung tissue slices
author: Khadim, Shahriari Felordi, et al.

steps.title: Prepare 2% ULMP agarose solution
steps.instruction: Make a 2 % (w/v) ultra‑low‑melting‑point agarose solution and keep it liquid until use.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 600 mg ULMP agarose and add to 30 mL sterile PBS in a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Secure the tube upright, cover the opening with plastic wrap and puncture a small hole for steam release.
Microwave the tube at 100 W until bubbles appear.
Remove and gently swirl to resuspend any undissolved agarose.
Re‑heat in short intervals until the solution reaches a gentle boil and becomes clear.
Swirl again to ensure uniform mixing.
Transfer the tube to a 37 °C incubator and keep the agarose liquid until needed.

steps.title: Clean instruments and anesthetize mouse
steps.instruction: Prepare all tools and deeply anesthetize the animal before any dissection.

substeps.instruction: Clean all surgical instruments thoroughly with an enzymatic detergent (e.g., Helizyme).
Induce deep anesthesia using isoflurane or an approved chemical anesthetic until loss of pedal reflex is confirmed.

steps.title: Position and disinfect mouse
steps.instruction: Place the anesthetized mouse in a supine position and sterilize the surgical area.

substeps.instruction: Place the mouse supine on a dissection board and secure limbs with tape or pins.
Disinfect the thoracic region with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Open thoracic cavity
steps.instruction: Expose the heart and lungs by cutting through the skin and rib cage.

substeps.instruction: Make a midline skin incision from abdomen to neck.
Cut through the rib cage to open the thoracic cavity and reveal the heart and lungs.

steps.title: Perfuse lungs via right ventricle
steps.instruction: Flush the pulmonary circulation to remove blood and blanch the lungs.

substeps.instruction: Insert a 25 G needle into the right ventricle.
Perfuse with 10–20 mL of 1× HBSS pre‑warmed to 37 °C (PBS may be used as an alternative).
Simultaneously snip the left atrium to allow blood to drain.
Continue until the lungs turn completely white, indicating effective perfusion.

steps.title: Cannulate trachea
steps.instruction: Insert a catheter into the airway to enable agarose instillation.

substeps.instruction: Insert a blunted 20 G catheter into the trachea.
Secure the catheter with a suture thread.

steps.title: Instill low‑melting agarose
steps.instruction: Inflate the lung with agarose to provide structural support for slicing.

substeps.instruction: Warm the 2 % low‑melting‑point agarose (prepared earlier) to 37 °C.
Slowly instill 1–2 mL of agarose via the tracheal catheter until the lobes are inflated but not over‑distended.
Clamp or tie the trachea to prevent backflow.
Allow the agarose to solidify for 10–15 min.
Place the filled lung in a 50 mL Falcon tube containing cold sterile medium or buffer to maintain sterility and accelerate solidification.

steps.title: Dissect and rinse lung
steps.instruction: Remove the solidified lung tissue and wash it in cold buffer.

substeps.instruction: Carefully dissect out the lung after agarose solidification.
Rinse the lung in cold sterile HBSS.

steps.title: Antigen retrieval of PCLS
steps.instruction: Unmask epitopes in the slices using heated citrate buffer with detergents.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑heat sodium citrate buffer to 80–85 °C.
Cool the buffer to 37 °C in a water bath and add 1 % Triton X‑100 and 1 % Tween‑20.
Submerge the PCLS in the lukewarm buffer for 30 min, keeping the buffer at 37 °C throughout.

steps.title: Wash after retrieval
steps.instruction: Remove retrieval buffer from the slices.

substeps.instruction: Wash the PCLS two times with 1× PBS, 5 min each, on a gentle rocking platform.

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Incubate slices in blocking solution to reduce background staining.

substeps.instruction: Incubate slices in 1× PBS containing 5 % BSA for 1 h at 18–28 °C with gentle rocking.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Bind anti‑ACTA2 and anti‑MKI‑67 antibodies to their targets.

substeps.instruction: Prepare anti‑ACTA2 and anti‑MKI‑67 antibodies in blocking buffer at 1:200 dilution.
Incubate slices either 8 h at 4 °C with gentle rocking, or 4 h at 18–28 °C in a humidified chamber (static).
Wash the PCLS three times with 1× PBS, 10 min each.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Apply fluorescent secondary antibody to visualize primary binding.

substeps.instruction: Prepare anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 647‑conjugated secondary antibody in blocking buffer at 1:1000 dilution.
Incubate slices for 2 h at 18–28 °C, protected from light.
Wash the PCLS three times with 1× PBS, 10 min each.

steps.title: DAPI nuclear staining
steps.instruction: Label nuclei with DAPI for fluorescence imaging.

substeps.instruction: Incubate slices with DAPI diluted 1:5000 in 1× PBS for 10 min.
Wash once with 1× PBS.

steps.title: Store or image slices
steps.instruction: Preserve stained slices or proceed to microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Either image immediately, or store at 4 °C in 0.05 % sodium azide dissolved in sterile 1× PBS.

description: The development of PCLS has transformed experimental lung research by enabling investigations in viable, structurally intact tissue that retains native cellular interactions and responses.2 Before starting this protocol, carefully consider the specific research objectives and the parameters that may affect slice viability and staining quality such as mouse age, strain, and health status. All reagents, including freshly prepared low-melting agarose and cold buffers, should be available, and slicing equipment must be clean and calibrated in advance. Slices generated by this protocol can be immediately used for fixed or live imaging, short-term cultures, or stimulation assays, making the method adaptable for diverse applications, from studying acute injury to testing therapeutics. Animal welfare and scientific rigor are foundational to this process. All procedures involving live animals must strictly adhere to local and national ethical regulations. Ensure protocols for anesthesia, perfusion, and euthanasia are both effective and humane, minimizing procedural artifacts. Aim to maximize tissue yield from each animal; one mouse lung can yield dozens of slices, thus reduce overall animal use and support the principles of 3R (Replacement, Reduction and Refinement). Planning these steps carefully ensures reproducibility and the highest ethical standards while enabling meaningful translational research.
